### CPI, PPI and cross-market reaction

**Release facts.** August CPI, released September 11 at 08:30 EDT: headline +0.4% m/m and +3.4% y/y; core +0.3% m/m and +2.4% y/y. July was +0.1%/+3.4% headline and +0.2%/+2.5% core. Gasoline +3.9% explained over one-third of the monthly headline rise; shelter accelerated from +0.1% to +0.3%. Annual core easing therefore coexists with firmer current monthly inflation. [BLS CPI](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/cpi.nr0.htm). Core +0.3% exceeded the +0.2% forecast in the timestamped MTFX/AMP calendars; headline matched +0.4%/+3.4%. A conflicting Kiplinger preview printed +0.4% core: this report discloses the disagreement and uses the corroborated calendar +0.2%, not the most convenient comparison.

August PPI, released September 10 at 08:30 EDT: final demand +0.4% m/m, +5.4% y/y, versus July +0.1%/+4.8%. Ex food/energy/trade services was +0.3%/+4.7%. This is a different exclusion basket from ordinary core PPI and must not be conflated with it. The annual headline exceeded the 5.3% median quoted by IBKR; its monthly +0.4% matched IBKR's forecast, although other surveys showed +0.3%. Energy was the main pressure, so calling every component uniformly hot would overstate the release. [BLS PPI](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_09102026.htm), [IBKR analysis](https://www.interactivebrokers.com/campus/traders-insight/ibkr-economic-landscape/hotter-than-expected-ppi-paired-with-wti-above-102-worsen-bond-market-meltdown/).

**Measured event windows.** Binance BTC/ETH use the last one-minute close before 08:30 EDT. Yahoo cross-market rows use the close of the 08:25–08:30 five-minute bar; subsequent five-minute bars are labelled by their END time. Yahoo is delayed; these are timestamped observations, not simultaneous executable quotes. Changes are from the event baseline, not the prior-day settlement.

At the latest delayed quote near 08:59 EDT, ES was 7675.50 (+0.28% versus its pre-CPI baseline, but +1.01% versus prior settlement), NQ 29474.50 (+0.29% event / +1.16% settlement), DXY 99.053, and Brent 104.56 versus prior settlement 107.63. At 08:54 EDT the 10-year yield was 4.928%, versus 4.949% pre-CPI and 4.944% prior close. These different baselines explain why a headline can say stocks are up 1% even though the measured post-CPI rise is much smaller. Cash S&P 500 had not opened at the evidence cutoff: 7591.70 is the September 10 CLOSE, not today's CPI response. SPY-universe breadth was 54.58% above the 200dma, with 502/505 names covered; it is descriptive breadth, not a live intraday advance/decline reading.

**Interpretation, not proven attribution.** PPI coincided with the conventional inflation-risk response: yields and dollar rose, bonds and equity futures fell, and crypto sold off. Oil/geopolitics and the same-day ECB decision are confounders; an event window cannot assign the whole move to PPI. CPI produced a sharp first-minute risk-off move, then a reversal across crypto, equities, the dollar and intermediate/long Treasuries. This supports a relief/positioning-unwind interpretation, rather than an all-clear on inflation. The two-year future's incomplete recovery matters: the maturity most sensitive to near-term policy still showed pressure while the long end recovered. Do not convert futures-price changes to yield changes without duration/CTD mapping, or claim an exact curve spread from unlike timestamps.

The mechanism is that firmer monthly inflation can keep policy restrictive, raising funding/discount rates and pressuring risk assets. A crowded defensive book can nevertheless rally when the feared outcome is absorbed and yields fail to sustain their first spike. Lower oil ahead of CPI was already helping futures; CPI alone did not create the entire rebound. Liquidation totals and post-release OI are not independently verified, so short covering is a plausible mechanism, not a measured fact.

**Broader macro remains restrictive.** FRED's last available real 10-year yield is 2.46% for Sep 9; breakeven inflation rose from 2.37% Sep 9 to 2.40% Sep 10; the two-year nominal yield was 4.43% Sep 9. These are dated daily observations, not post-CPI ticks, and cannot be subtracted from today's nominal yield to invent a current real rate. Brent above $100 keeps renewed energy pass-through a live risk. No current FedWatch probability is asserted: yesterday's roughly 70% hike estimate is not today's price. The next FOMC decision is Sep 16 at 14:00 EDT, press conference 14:30.

**Tests for the next session.** IF the 10-year stays below its 4.949% pre-CPI baseline, DXY stays below 99.135 and ES holds above 7653.75 after the cash open, THEN the relief interpretation gains support. Falsifier: sustained return above those yield/dollar baselines together with ES losing 7653.75. A break above the 4.985% event yield high with renewed oil strength would strengthen the restrictive-macro case, but still cannot waive either crypto asset's failed FR regime test. These are event anchors from Sep 11, not predictions of a resolved macro regime.

### Analyst Read

The largest information the old rubric misses today is the sequence: an inflation shock was initially sold, then failed to sustain across bonds, dollar, equity futures and crypto. That is evidence against chasing the first-minute selloff, while firmer monthly core CPI and costly oil remain medium-horizon headwinds. Strongest case against standing down is the persistent 24h/3d spot selling and ETF softness: the rally may fail after the cash open. Strongest contrary reading is that the adverse news has been absorbed while both assets remain above rising 200dma. The single structural input that changes routing is a completed move below a FALLING 200dma; price crossing today's MA alone is insufficient while its 20-session slope is positive. S1=0 and S2 unused: no bounded opinion can clear the regime, valuation preflight or minimum-edge veto.
